## Protein Workbench is the integrated protein-centric entry point

In the current **ProtVis 0.9.16** Toolkits menu, **Protein Workbench** is the first item. It resolves a single protein/gene/UniProt identifier or amino-acid sequence once, then reuses that context across annotation, PTM sites, domains, AlphaFold structure, localization, STRING interactions, plant evolutionary analysis and binding-pocket prediction.

Use the expandable [Protein Workbench](Protein_Workbench.qmd) documentation for the complete workflow:

**ID / sequence → UniProt/MaizeGDB → sequence/PTM/domains/structure → localization & interaction → evolution → binding pockets**

## Current toolkit map

| Toolkit | Main purpose |
|---|---|
| **Protein Workbench** | integrated protein-centric analysis hub |
| **Protein Extract** | extract protein sequences from FASTA by identifiers |
| **Plant-mPLoc** | plant subcellular-localization prediction |
| **Background Make** | build GO/KEGG background workbooks |
| **Protein Links** | UniProt/InterPro/SWISS-MODEL-oriented protein links and sequence search |
| **Protein Structure** | bio3d-based structure/NMA inspection |
| **Boxplot** | grouped quantitative boxplots and statistical comparison |
| **SwissModel** | dedicated SWISS-MODEL workflow |
| **STRINGdb PPI** | dedicated STRINGdb network workflow |
| **Stacked Column Diagram** | stacked/grouped/100% stacked categorical abundance plots |
| **Correlation chord** | correlation matrix and chord/network representation |
| **Transcriptome Analysis** | DESeq2 + PCA/volcano + maize KEGG GSEA workflow |
| **Release data** | export stage/project data from the running app |

## Integrated versus standalone tools

Protein Workbench intentionally overlaps several focused utilities without removing them. For example, it can call Plant-mPLoc for the current protein, query STRING partners, display AlphaFold structure and link to SWISS-MODEL; the standalone pages remain available when you want a dedicated interface or batch/independent workflow.

Recommended use:

- choose **Protein Workbench** when one candidate protein needs multi-angle interpretation;
- choose a **standalone toolkit** when the task is focused, independent of a resolved protein, or uses a specialized input/output workflow.

## Reproducibility

Toolkits that receive the shared active `ProtVis_dataset` append their completed analyses as schema-v4 toolkit runs where implemented. Keep exported FASTA/PDB/tables/figures and external-database settings together with the project when toolkit evidence contributes to a final biological conclusion.

External-resource modules depend on the availability and current APIs of services such as UniProt, InterPro, AlphaFold DB, MaizeGDB/MaizeMine, STRING and Plant-mPLoc. A network-service failure should be reported separately from local sequence/structure analysis.
